conjecture: Of the claim I sent Lyra -- 'the number survives, the attribution does not' -- half one holds unconditionally and half two holds conditional on the absence of a judge main effect. phi-bar is exactly the between-item share of error variance, so Kish's n_eff ceiling 1/phi-bar is set by an item functional; the item, not the judge, is the unit of replication.

tree.approach: The conjunction as sent to Lyra on 2026-09-30. Half one (the number) is proved unconditionally. Half two (the attribution) is proved under (ECI)(ii), whose failure mode omega2 > 0 is UNMEASURED on her data and invisible to the estimator she ran -- so the root stays in-progress rather than proved.

children.approach: Theorem 1. Under (ECI) -- i.i.d. items, errors conditionally independent and identically distributed across judges given the item state, finite second moments -- Cov(E_ij,E_ij')=tau2=Var(E[E|F_i]) and Var(E_ij)=tau2+sigma2, so phi-bar = tau2/(tau2+sigma2) exactly. Two applications of the law of total (co)variance; NO distributional assumption, so it holds verbatim for binary errors (conditional Bernoulli) as well as the additive Gaussian model. Corollary: the numerator of phi-bar is the variance of a function of the ITEM alone -- the judge index does not occur in it. This one line is the whole re-attribution.

Corollary 1.1/1.2. n_eff(J)=J/(1+(J-1)phi-bar) is strictly increasing in J (derivative (1-p)/(1+(J-1)p)^2) and n_eff(J) < 1/phi-bar = 1 + sigma2/tau2 for every finite J. So the honest headline is 'no panel size buys more than about two', not 'nine buys two'. Her 1.99 is 97.5 percent of the ceiling 2.041 at phi-bar=0.49, i.e. a saturation value.

Corollary 1.3, and the mechanism that makes the ceiling feel inevitable. E[Ebar_i | F_i] = m(F_i) independent of J, so m(F_i) is a BIAS of the measurement on item i: E[(Xbar_i - theta_i)^2 | F_i] = m(F_i)^2 + s2(F_i)/J. The co-failure is not nine opinions collapsing into two; it is nine independent measurements of an OFFSET quantity. Averaging kills variance and leaves bias untouched -- which is what a ceiling looks like from the inside. Hence: Kish's design effect cannot distinguish redundancy from bias, and on alphaNLI it is reporting bias.

Theorem 2. Var(M) = (v+tau2)/I + sigma2/(IJ) + omega2/J, by independence of the four mean-zero components of M = thetabar + ubar + wbar + ebar. The asymmetry that does all the work: the INDEX SET of a variance component dictates which count shrinks it -- u is indexed by i so ubar averages I terms, w is indexed by j so wbar averages J terms. Corollaries: inf_J Var(M) = (v+tau2)/I > 0 with exactly sigma2/(IJ) still purchasable by growing the panel; and (if omega2=0) Var(M) -> 0 as I -> infinity for every fixed J including J=1. Verified by symbolic expansion of E[M^2] (difference exactly 0 at five (I,J) pairs) and 4000/4000 on a randomised grid, worst relative error 3.7e-16.

Theorem 3, and the deliverable that replaces the conditional exchange rate. At fixed total judgments B=IJ, substituting I=B/J gives Var(M) = (J(v+tau2)+sigma2)/B, strictly increasing in J whenever v+tau2>0, so J=1 minimises it UNCONDITIONALLY -- no inequality to check, no dataset dependence, and it survives dropping v (fixed item set: replace v+tau2 by tau2, derivative still positive). With omega2>0 the objective is strictly convex with interior minimiser J* = sqrt(omega2 B/(v+tau2)); integer argmin matches (7 vs 6.71, 21 vs 21.21).

Theorem 5, replacing the withdrawn Prop 4. Kish's 1/phi-bar is the design effect for the ERROR variance: per-item MSE about the truth (tau2+sigma2/J -> tau2) and identically the error component of Var(M) ((tau2+sigma2/J)/I -> tau2/I) have the SAME ratio 1/phi-bar. It is NOT the design effect for total Var(M), which also carries the irreducible item-sampling term v/I (ranges 1.01 to 2.00 across parameter sets while 1/phi-bar stays 2.00). So aggregate and per-item ESTIMATION share one ceiling. The genuine divergence Lyra observed is estimation (ceiling 1/phi-bar) versus DETECTION (no ceiling: E[p_i^J] -> 0, decaying as J^-b for p_i ~ Beta(a,b), polynomially rather than geometrically). Mechanism: bias caps estimation because averaging cannot move an offset; bias does not cap a disjunction over judges, because detection needs only one judge on the right side of a threshold and conditional independence is intact for that purpose.

Theorem 6, answering her second question. (a) Raw-score ESDOF is the participation ratio of (v+tau2)11^T + sigma2 Id, hence a function of (v+tau2)/sigma2 ONLY -- a signal-to-noise ratio. It equals J when v+tau2=0 and equals 1 exactly when sigma2=0, i.e. it is MINIMISED by a panel of perfect judges; a reliability statistic minimised by perfect judges is measuring signal, not reliability. So: errors, and for identifiability, not 'for consistency' (consistency would be equally served by moving Kish onto raw scores, which would be wrong). (b) Error ESDOF is a function of (J, phi-bar) alone. (c) The two statistics she prints as n_eff have DIFFERENT ceilings: sum(lambda)=J exactly while sum(lambda^2) ~ J^2 phi-bar^2, so ESDOF -> 1/phi-bar^2 against Kish's 1/phi-bar -- 4.16 vs 2.04 on her panel, 3.08 vs 1.83 at J=9. Kish is the variance effective-n (it IS the design-effect ratio); the participation ratio counts spectral dimensions and appears in no variance formula. Recommend renaming it away from n_eff. Minor bug: both of her functions return nan silently on a panel with no error variance (keep-mask drops every column, 0/0).

The re-attribution WITHOUT a side condition -- i.e. 'the item is the unit of replication' full stop, which is what Lyra would print in a headline. This is the node that is not closed, and the only blocker in the document.

Theorem 4, the enemy located. In (M2) X_ij = theta_i + u_i + w_j + e_ij: (a) the mean off-diagonal of np.corrcoef on error columns targets tau2/(tau2+sigma2), FREE of omega2, because Pearson correlation centres each column at its own mean and a per-judge additive shift is annihilated by that centring -- phi_hat reads 0.5001 for omega2 in {0,0.25,1,4,25}; (b) Kish's n_eff built from it is nonetheless the correct design effect for the error variance of the panel mean conditional on the realised panel, so HALF ONE SURVIVES omega2 unconditionally; (c) but Var(M) gains omega2/J, so inf_I Var(M) = omega2/J > 0 and 'I has no floor' is FALSE when omega2>0 (for a fixed panel, wbar is instead a constant bias of M, equally unremovable by I). The shape of the danger: the instrument she ran cannot see the quantity that would refute the conclusion drawn from it.

The empirical premise the unconditional re-attribution needs: omega2 (between-judge variance of per-judge mean error) is negligible relative to tau2 on the ChaosNLI alphaNLI panel. UNMEASURED. Her reported phi-bar=0.49 is compatible with omega2=0 and with omega2=25 alike, so her existing measurement cannot supply it. The test is a one-way ANOVA on the column means of her error matrix, omega2_hat = Var_j(column mean) - (tau2+sigma2)_hat/I; she has the data and I do not (the repo at 3fa2760 holds the draft, the tex and the build script, no alphaNLI data). Three outcomes give three different headlines: omega2~0 clean re-attribution; omega2 << tau2 re-attribution with a stated remainder and J* from the budget theorem; omega2 >= tau2 the ceiling is SHARED, not relocated.

WITHDRAWN. My brief's Prop 4: 'for a per-item estimand the relevant variance is Var(Xbar_i|i)=sigma2/J, so J judges are worth nearly J; same panel, same data, two n_eff's differing by about four.' Superseded by one-ceiling-for-estimation.
children.reason: Conditioning on the item removes u_i -- but u_i IS the error. What is left, Var(Xbar_i | F_i) = sigma2/J, measures the panel's precision about its own BIASED CONSENSUS, which is nobody's estimand. For accuracy about the truth, per-item MSE (tau2+sigma2/J) and the error component of Var(M) have the SAME design effect 1/phi-bar. So there are not two n_eff's differing by four; there is one estimation ceiling. The real divergence is estimation vs detection -- a distinction Lyra had ALREADY drawn in the article, so this also corrects an over-claim of novelty on my part.

children.approach: My brief's Prop 3: infinitely many judges on I items beats one judge on 2I items iff v+tau2 < sigma2. The iff is correct and proved. But it compares two DIFFERENT budgets (infinity against 2I), which is why it is conditional, and it is framing-dependent: on her implied parameters the sampled-item framing gives v+tau2=4.70 > sigma2=1 (one judge on 2I items wins by 4.7x) while the fixed-item framing gives tau2=0.99 < sigma2=1 (infinite judges wins by 1 percent, break-even being exactly phi-bar=1/2, and her phi-bar=0.4975 sits on the knife edge). Kept as a true but superseded attempt: fixed-budget-optimum is the statement to send.

Over-identification check on her three reported numbers (49 percent between-item, raw n_eff 1.21, error n_eff 1.99). Theorem 1 says the first IS phi-bar, so they constrain each other. Inverting Kish (J = t(1-p)/(1-tp)) at p=0.49 gives n_eff=1.99 iff J ~ 41; at J=9, phi-bar=0.49 yields 1.829, and n_eff=1.99 at J=9 would require phi-bar=0.4403, contradicting the reported 49 percent. So the 1.99 and the 49 percent are mutually consistent only if the panel has J >~ 40. Taking J=100 (full ChaosNLI annotator set) gives phi-bar=0.4975, which rounds to her 49 percent as a PREDICTION rather than a fit, and (v,tau2,sigma2)=(3.71,0.99,1.00) reproduces 1.21 and 1.99 simultaneously. J is INFERRED, not read -- flagged to her for confirmation.

Textual finding at 3fa2760. The sentence 'correlating raw label indices ON THIS PANEL gives n_eff ~ 1.2 ... the error-based version gives ~ 2.0' reports numbers measured on ChaosNLI alphaNLI (per mail UID 742), but grep -ci 'alphanli|chaosnli' returns 0 in BOTH _article.tex and DRAFT-2026-09-11.md: the dataset is never named in the article. The nearest antecedent for 'this panel' is Kohli's nine frontier LLM judges from the opening paragraph. A crowd-annotator measurement on an NLI benchmark therefore reads as a measurement on the nine-LLM panel, and because 2.0 and Kohli's 2.18 agree in MAGNITUDE nothing in the text makes the substitution visible. The arithmetic confirms they cannot be the same object: phi-bar=0.49 at J=9 gives 1.83, not 1.99. Recommended fix: name the dataset and the J in that sentence.
